title.en: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers
A visit that left a deep mark

text.en: Homage means something said or done to show respect publicly for someone. In this chapter two friends, Soumya and Ananda, exchange letters about a visit to the National War Memorial in New Delhi and the gratitude every Indian owes to the soldiers who protect us.

You think about whom every Indian should pay homage to, and in pairs list three ways to celebrate soldiers' victories and three ways to honour their sacrifices, such as visiting a war memorial.
Soumya writes from Jayanagar, Bengaluru, on 14 April to her friend Ananda. She recalls their talk about war and peace and how India struggled for centuries to win Independence from the British. After Independence India has had to fight several wars to protect its borders, its territorial integrity, which means safeguarding the nation's borders, and its people. She wondered who these brave people were, and on a school trip to New Delhi she found some answers.
Its construction began in April 2018 and was completed in February 2019. It was envisioned, meaning visualised, and inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. It is spread over 40 acres near the iconic India Gate. The teacher explained that freedom and security exist because brave men and women of the Armed Forces served for decades, and that war always takes its toll. Such monuments remind us never to forget the cost of freedom. Each brick is a tablet bearing the names of soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice from 1947 till date, including the 1962 Indo-China conflict, the 1965 and 1971 Indo-Pak wars and the 1999 Kargil War. There are 29,000 tablets with more than 26,000 names etched, which means engraved, on them.
21 bravehearts were awarded the Param Vir Chakra, India's highest wartime gallantry medal. Other awards are the Maha Vir Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Vir Chakra and Shaurya Chakra. Major Somnath Sharma received the first Param Vir Chakra, posthumously, which means after death, for the Battle of Badgam in 1947. A PVC was also awarded for service in the UN Peace Keeping Operations in Congo. Captain Mahendra Nath Mulla was among those given the Maha Vir Chakra. Lance Naik Albert Ekka, 14 Guards, was awarded the PVC for the attack at Gangasagar on the eastern front. He silenced two enemy machine guns at great risk and was fatally injured. His citation, which is a statement of meritorious performance of duty, left Soumya awestruck, meaning amazed, and she wished to be as courageous when she joins the Army.
Amar Jawan Jyoti is an immortal flame kept burning day and night in honour of the soldiers. It was first lit under the arch of India Gate in January 1972 to commemorate the 1971 victory. It now stands in the obelisk, a tapering stone pillar, of the memorial, and the old flame was merged with the new one. The memorial has four concentric circles around a 15-metre-tall central obelisk. The innermost is Amar Chakra, the Circle of Immortality, with the eternal flame. The second is Veerta Chakra, the Circle of Bravery, a covered gallery with six bronze murals of valiant battle actions. The third is Tyag Chakra, the Circle of Sacrifice, whose walls recall the ancient Chakravyuh formation and carry granite tablets with names in golden letters, one for each fallen hero of post-Independent India. The outermost is Raksha Chakra, the Circle of Protection, a row of trees where each tree represents a soldier guarding the nation. Soumya spent the whole day there around the lawns of Kartavyapath. The solemn atmosphere moved her to tears and made her want to live a life worthy of the heroes' sacrifice.
Back at school the class formed five groups to present stories of valour, and Soumya chose Major Padmapani Acharya of 2 Rajputana Rifles, awarded the Maha Vir Chakra after his death in the 1999 Kargil War. On 28 June 1999, as Company Commander, he was ordered to capture a heavily fortified enemy position. Though his leading platoon suffered heavy casualties, he led the reserve platoon up the steep rock face through artillery fire, crawled to the enemy position and threw grenades. Badly wounded, he ordered his men to leave him and charge while he kept firing. The objective was captured, but he died of his injuries. Before battle he wrote to his father that he was not afraid of losing his life for the motherland, and quoted the Bhagavad Gita on being ready to fight, whether the result is victory or death.
Ananda writes from Chandigarh on 24 April. She praises Soumya's eye for detail and sensitivity. She says a war memorial is not just an edifice, a large impressive building, but an expression of deep gratitude for the supreme sacrifice of soldiers defending the sovereignty and integrity of the country. She feels motivated to think of joining the Armed Forces. She recalls visiting a memorial in the Bougainvillea Garden in Sector 3, Chandigarh, where people offered flowers, and shares a poem by Makhanlal Chaturvedi about a flower that wishes to be thrown on the path where brave men go to give their heads for the motherland. She also mentions Captain Anuj Nayyar of 17 Jat, who was posthumously awarded the Maha Vir Chakra, India's second highest gallantry award, for valour in the Kargil War.
Which is India's highest gallantry award? The Param Vir Chakra. How would Ananda feel? Inspired and proud, as she herself says she is motivated to serve. Soumya clearly enjoyed writing: she calls it a long letter, says she could not help sharing the experience, and ends with friendly remarks about food and family. Feelings in the text include wonder at the memorial, sadness at the loss of life, gratitude for freedom and pride in the nation.

problem.en: Match each Chakra with its meaning.

text.en: Amar Chakra.

why.en: Circle of Immortality, with the eternal flame.

text.en: Raksha Chakra.

why.en: Circle of Protection, the row of trees.

problem.en: Why is Amar Jawan Jyoti described as immortal?

text.en: What does the flame do?
What does it symbolise?

why.en: The spirit of fallen soldiers is immortal and the nation will not forget them.

prompt.en: Explain why the National War Memorial is important and what the letters teach us.

requiredIdeas.en: It lists the names of soldiers who gave their lives after 1947.
It reminds us of the cost of freedom and the horrors of war.
Soumya and Ananda show gratitude and inspire others to serve.
We should honour the soldiers by remembering and by being worthy citizens.

commonMisconceptions.en: It honours only those who won the Param Vir Chakra.

points.en: The National War Memorial near India Gate honours soldiers who died after 1947.
It has four Chakras: Amar, Veerta, Tyag and Raksha.
Soumya presents the story of Major Padmapani Acharya.
The letters express gratitude and inspire service.
Words such as gallantry, posthumously and commemorate build our vocabulary.
